summary: The Phase 2 security review passes at the unchanged phase tree 1902a8215. Live IAM confirms the www deploy key no longer holds direct Cloud Run write access or project-level actAs. An authorized key holder can still submit a custom build as the privileged default build account. The PM records that residual risk for Phase 4. No workflow starts a traffic file. Sales release inputs fail closed until the PM chooses a backup time and input path.
nonblocking_findings: N1 [Nit] apps/accounting, apps/codecamp-advantage, apps/sales-advantage: fixed traffic tags can point to a later push. Sales captures _PUSH_BUILD_ID but moves the candidate tag. Task 3.3a requires sales to bind both to the same build before traffic runs. The other fixed-tag limits remain in docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md.

N2 [Nit] Cloud Build IAM: a holder of the GitHub deploy key can submit a custom build as each project's privileged default build account. The www default account retains editor, run.admin, storage.admin, and actAs; a build can move traffic despite the key's direct Cloud Run grants being removed. The PM records dedicated build accounts and WIF under task 4.7. No production build or privilege test ran in this review.

N3 [Nit] deploy IAM: roles/storage.bucketViewer remains project-wide in www, primary-advantage, and reading-advantage. The latter two also retain project-wide logging.viewer. Task 4.7 records the www bucket and log-scope reduction.

N4 [Nit] gated Cloud Run revisions: --no-traffic does not make a revision private. A tagged revision with --allow-unauthenticated remains reachable at the tag URL with production secrets and database access. The design risk remains documented.

N6 [Nit] workbooks runtime: the planned service account still needs secretmanager.secretAccessor on WORKBOOKS_DATABASE_URL and WORKBOOKS_COMPANY_AUTH_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET when those secrets exist. Task 2.3i defers the first workbooks release and records that the current job fails closed.

The current audited phase paths equal the supplied role base.

Security applies: test-strategy.md lines 118-125 and 571-578 rate P2 critical and require Review B. The phase diff adds two CD workflows and manual traffic files and changes deploy and database steps. The diff also contains other tracks; this audit stays on the listed phase paths.

B1 withdrawn: live www project policy binds www-reading-github only to cloudbuild.builds.editor, serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer, and storage.bucketViewer. The build bucket binds objectCreator and objectViewer. The compute account grants serviceAccountUser to this member. The www Cloud Run service grants run.viewer. The prior direct no-build deploy and traffic path through project editor/run.admin and project-wide actAs no longer exists. Task 2.6 and task 4.7 record the reduction and the remaining indirect build risk.

The www default build account is 909092567806-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com. Its live project roles include editor, run.admin, storage.admin, iam.serviceAccountUser, artifactregistry.writer, and logging.logWriter. The GitHub key has builds.editor and can act as this specific account, so a custom build remains a privileged path. This is not a direct no-build path. Phase 4 must prove the normal www CD build with the reduced key; this read-only review cannot prove it.

Primary and Reading project policies still bind the deploy identity only to cloudbuild.builds.editor, logging.viewer, serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer, and storage.bucketViewer. The prior review verified each build bucket's objectCreator/objectViewer grants. No direct run role appears in either project's current member bindings.

Injection and input boundaries: cd-apps.yml lines 43-76 read BASE_SHA and HEAD_SHA from push event metadata through environment variables. affected-apps.mjs validates full 40-hex refs. The matrix comes from committed scripts/ci/apps.json. The new substitutions field is either empty or --substitutions=_RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA=<github.sha>. The latter is an event commit SHA, not an untrusted message or PR title. Its unquoted shell interpolation cannot add a shell operator from that value. The submit still fails on a missing config.

Marketing gets the pushed commit because its push file declares exactly one REQUIRED_ default, _RELEASE_COMMIT_SHA. Sales declares three REQUIRED_ defaults, so its matrix field is empty and validate-release-inputs rejects the defaults. The runbook names this open limit. No backup time, release input, or approval is inferred or supplied.

Secrets and permissions: both workflows run only for a push to master and declare contents: read. The only secret references are GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT and GCP_PROJECT_ID. No pull_request_target trigger, write-all, log of secret content, or workflow invocation of a traffic file appears. Cloud Build files mount named secrets only in the steps that require them; the diff contains no private key text.

Persistence and errors: the six manual traffic files move traffic only by --to-tags, after database checks. The three variable-tag files require _TAG with no default, and sales requires _PUSH_BUILD_ID with no default. docs/runbooks/traffic-moves.md identifies fixed-tag drift and the backup guard. Push workflows do not call traffic files. Initial accounting deployment has a separate first-service rule; no existing service traffic moves on a push.

N5 resolved: both workflows pin all ten uses lines to four 40-hex action commits with version comments (a60c8352c); Review A independently checked tag targets. N7 resolved: measure/tracks.md line 79 now says Phase 2 in review remediation (9e10c5bad). N1 remains open for fixed accounting and codecamp tags; task 3.3a covers sales. N2 and N3 remain assigned to task 4.7. N4 remains a documented design limit. N6 remains deferred to task 2.3i.

A2 does not apply: the scoped phase paths build and deploy containers; no draft-to-published test or transition occurs. A6 holds: the track row in measure/tracks.md claims Phase 2 review remediation, not a resolved security state. No green adversarial security claim appears in that row. Other unrelated tracks' registry statements are outside this phase.

Review A at review-a-1902a8215.json reports 119 passing targeted tests, including 107 scripts/ci tests, and a known sales approval failure of one test. This audit ran read-only IAM and static security checks; it did not run a build or change credentials.
